name: tabular_online_sgd
title: Out-of-core click prediction: partial_fit over read_csv chunks, a hash-bucket holdout and no fit() or train_test_split anywhere
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the streaming / incremental-learning false-positive trap

forbidden.why: scaler.partial_fit at line 44 is given train_x, which stream.chunks() already separated from the holdout rows at stream.py:36-38; the holdout is only ever transform()ed, at lines 45 and 49
stream.py fits nothing: it reads chunks, computes a hash bucket and slices the frame
holdout_x reaches scaler.transform at line 49 and nothing else; partial_fit is called only on train_x. A PARTIAL_FIT role is not a leak by itself - incremental learning is what partial_fit is for
no transformer is touched in stream.py
there is no cross_val_score / cross_validate / *SearchCV call in this project; every pass over the data refits the scaler state chunk by chunk
`hour` is an integer hour-of-day feature; nothing parses a date, converts one or sorts by one, and the holdout is a hash bucket rather than a random draw
hash_holdout is a modulo on an integer row id - deterministic, order-independent and not a shuffle
the only metrics are roc_auc_score and log_loss, both in the score-metric carve-out, and both are fed a predict_proba column
roc_auc_score at line 55 is fed model.predict_proba(...)[:, 1] from line 49, a score column rather than a hard label
seed_everything() seeds random and numpy at lines 30-31 and SGDClassifier carries random_state=SEED
there is no splitter object in this project at all: the holdout comes from a deterministic hash bucket, which needs no random_state and cannot take one
hash_holdout has no randomness to seed
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step; the epoch loop drives partial_fit, not backward()
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no sklearn equivalent, and the loop at line 42 is a training pass rather than an evaluation loop
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a scikit-learn program
no device is ever named in this project
there is no torch DataLoader here; the chunk generator yields the file's own order on purpose, because an out-of-core pass cannot shuffle what it has not read

notes: The honest defect this project does NOT have, and which no rule covers, is that `scaler.partial_fit` keeps updating across epochs, so the holdout rows of epoch 2 are transformed by a state that has already seen epoch 1's training rows. That is correct for online learning - the state is meant to be cumulative - and is recorded here so the distinction is on the record.
